question: Should OpenClaw accept this phase-one Codex supervision boundary—snapshot branches for local stored or idle sessions, local archive with explicit fencing, paired-node read-only metadata, and the associated public session runtime seams—once real setup and upgrade proof is supplied?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and upstream-aligned, but accepting a new persisted-session and plugin API contract plus this security boundary is a product and ownership decision that automated review cannot make.

options.title: Approve phase one after proof
options.body: Accept the current boundary after a real fresh-install workflow and a legacy `codex-supervisor` doctor migration both demonstrate the documented behavior.

options.title: Narrow the initial surface
options.body: Land catalog and local continuation first while deferring archive or delegated-execution API exposure to a separately reviewed change.

options.title: Defer supervision integration
options.body: Keep the existing read-only catalog until maintainers are ready to own the broader session, migration, and security contracts.

recommendation.title: Approve phase one after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the current boundary after a real fresh-install workflow and a legacy `codex-supervisor` doctor migration both demonstrate the documented behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the merged catalog foundation and authored the canonical product direction for interactive Codex supervision.
